incident.summary: Cronos validators halted the network after an exploit affected Tectonic, a lending protocol on Cronos. Public reporting places the preliminary affected amount around USD 74-75 million, with roughly USD 6 million bridged to Ethereum before the halt. Tectonic and Cronos had not confirmed a final loss amount or formal root cause at review time.
incident.preliminary_mechanism: Reported on-chain analysis indicates manipulation of the low-liquidity TONIC token price followed by borrowing against inflated collateral. Treat this as a preliminary mechanism until formally confirmed.
incident.funds_status: Most exploit-linked assets were reported as stranded on Cronos after the halt. Do not describe stranded/frozen funds as recovered unless recovery is later confirmed.

hei_decision.reason: Tectonic is a lending-only protocol and is not an exchange, DEX, or hybrid exchange entity under the current HEI scope.
hei_decision.follow_up_action: Identify any HEI-covered Cronos-based DEX/exchange with documented trading, swap, deposit, withdrawal, or service interruption caused by the Cronos halt. Only then stage an exchange-specific event with direct evidence.
hei_decision.crypto_com_note: Reporting states the Crypto.com app and exchange were not compromised. Do not infer a Crypto.com exchange incident solely from the Cronos chain halt.

evidence.title: Crypto.com-linked Cronos network halts after Tectonic exploit estimated at $75 million
evidence.notes: Supports Cronos halt, preliminary approximately USD 75M estimate, approximately USD 6M bridged, preliminary manipulation mechanism, and statement that Crypto.com app/exchange were not compromised.

evidence.title: Cronos halts blockchain after $75 million lending exploit hits lending app Tectonic
evidence.notes: Supports the chain halt, preliminary approximately USD 75M estimate, TONIC price-manipulation framing, and lack of confirmed final loss/restart timetable at publication time.

evidence.title: Tectonic Exploited on Cronos for Estimated $75 Million as Validators Halt Entire Network
evidence.notes: Supports that Tectonic acknowledged the incident, the approximately USD 75M figure remained preliminary, and the final loss/root cause had not been formally confirmed.

review_checklist: Do not create Tectonic as an HEI entity.
Do not mark any HEI entity dead, limited, hacked, or withdrawal-suspended from this incident without exchange-specific evidence.
Search HEI-covered Cronos DEX/exchange entities for documented user-facing interruption during the halt.
If a specific exchange-side interruption is confirmed, stage only that event and its direct evidence.
Keep loss amount explicitly preliminary until Tectonic/Cronos publishes a final figure.
Do not equate frozen or stranded attacker-controlled assets with recovered funds.
